title: FIXTURE: The Orchard School Lunch Incident
content_warning: This fictional fixture describes a serious allergic reaction involving a child.

question.prompt: How much of the blame for the incident falls on the school district?

starting_facts.text: A student had an allergic reaction at the fictional Orchard School cafeteria in March 2026.
The student recovered after treatment at a hospital.
The family has filed a civil complaint against the district and the food vendor.

steps.headline: The menu card did not list peanuts as an ingredient.
steps.body: Photos filed with the complaint show the day's menu card. Peanuts are not listed. This is a fictional test fixture.

steps.headline: The vendor changed its sauce recipe a week earlier.
steps.body: The vendor's own change log shows a new sauce supplier on March 2. The district says it was not told. This is a fictional test fixture.

depth.title: Vendor change log
depth.summary: Lists a supplier change for the sauce on March 2.

steps.headline: Staff used an epinephrine pen within four minutes.
steps.body: The district's incident log records the time of the first call and the injection. The two are four minutes apart. This is a fictional test fixture.

steps.headline: Two of five cafeteria staff had lapsed allergy training.
steps.body: State records show two certifications expired in 2025. The district says renewals were scheduled. This is a fictional test fixture.

depth.title: What the state requires
depth.body: The fictional state rule requires annual allergy-response training for cafeteria staff.

steps.headline: The allergy form on file was from a previous school year.
steps.body: The district says the family's allergy form had not been renewed. The family's lawyer says the district never asked for a new one. This is a fictional test fixture.

depth.text: Nobody from the school ever asked us to update anything.
depth.speaker: Family's lawyer (fictional)

steps.headline: Neighboring districts require vendors to report recipe changes.
steps.body: An education policy group surveyed nearby districts. Four of six require written notice of recipe changes. This is a fictional test fixture.

sides.label: The district failed
sides.steelman: The district let training lapse and had no rule requiring vendors to report recipe changes.

sides.label: The vendor failed
sides.steelman: The vendor changed an ingredient source without telling anyone.

sides.label: Responsibility is shared
sides.steelman: Paperwork gaps on all sides, including the family's, let this happen.

open_questions: Did the vendor send any notice that the district did not receive?
Will the state audit the district's training records?

sources.title: Civil complaint (fixture)
sources.quote_excerpt: The menu card provided no warning of peanut content.
